taskDescription: A farmer is brought to casualty after drinking an organophosphate pesticide. Arrange the steps of poisoning and treatment in the correct sequence.
paragraphs: The organophosphate covalently phosphorylates the active-site serine of acetylcholinesterase, irreversibly inhibiting the enzyme.
Acetylcholine accumulates at cholinergic synapses because it can no longer be hydrolysed.
Excess acetylcholine overstimulates muscarinic receptors, causing miosis, salivation, bronchospasm and bradycardia.
Atropine is given to block the excess muscarinic stimulation at receptor level.
Pralidoxime is given early to reactivate the phosphorylated enzyme before the phosphoryl group ages and the bond becomes permanent.

overallFeedback.feedback: Organophosphates irreversibly inhibit acetylcholinesterase by phosphorylating its active-site serine → acetylcholine accumulates → muscarinic overstimulation produces the cholinergic toxidrome. Atropine blocks the muscarinic effects while pralidoxime must be given before 'aging' to cleave the phosphoryl group, because once aged, only new enzyme synthesis restores activity.
